units.function: Comprehensive AWS Secrets Manager provider tests for managed and externally linked Secrets, SigV4 requests, namespace isolation, rotation, metadata-only discovery, error redaction, version resolution, health, deletion/recovery and rollback of write-through changes.
units.dependencyDirection: SecretService-facing provider methods receive provider-vault config, Secret value/context and stored provider material; a gateway or built-in signed HTTP client calls AWS APIs. Only opaque ARN/version/hash/material returns to persistence, while plaintext crosses the provider boundary transiently for create, update or resolve.
units.keyDataModels: AWS region/endpoint/credentials/KMS key, deployment/prefix/Company namespace and tags, managed versus external-reference material, ARN, AWS VersionId/VersionStage, PAPERCLIP_PENDING/AWSCURRENT, previous and last-written versions, provider vault candidate, metadata pagination, health warning and redacted client error.
units.lifecycle: Managed creation derives an exact deployment/Company name and optional KMS key, with later versions staged pending and out-of-scope refs rejected. External references store metadata only; optional write-through captures current version, publishes a new AWSCURRENT and records rollback ids. Listing/discovery never calls GetSecretValue and filters foreign managed samples. Resolution may pin a version and revalidates managed namespace. Managed deletion uses a recovery window; archive removes pending stage, while external rollback moves AWSCURRENT back to the prior version.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen unusually strong provider tests cover plaintext non-persistence, selected-vault isolation from env fallback, request signing/timeout signal, namespace drift, managed/external ownership separation, metadata-only discovery, redacted public errors, version-pinned resolution, configuration health, deletion safety and rollback semantics. Missing are real AWS/LocalStack contract tests, binary Secrets, credential refresh/IMDS failure, retries/throttling/idempotency tokens, endpoint/account/partition validation, KMS policy/grants, tag spoofing, pagination limits, concurrent rotations/CAS, partial network outcomes, deletion restoration, zeroization and proof that rawMessage is never logged or serialized.
units.designRationale: Support both Company-owned managed Secret lifecycle and existing enterprise vault references without copying values into the control database, while defending provider ownership boundaries and offering reversible operations and safe discovery UX.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a provider-neutral Secret custody port spanning managed cloud and customer-local vaults, with explicit ownership, immutable grant/audit evidence, purpose-bound delivery and safe coexistence with enterprise rotation systems.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider contract, managed/external ownership split, namespace revalidation on every operation, metadata-only discovery, recovery window, structured redaction and version material. Use the official AWS SDK/credential chain rather than owning SigV4 transport unless proven necessary. Require KMS/profile policy, account/partition allowlists, idempotency/CAS, transactional operation journal and execution-node leases tied to Work, Connector, purpose, expiry and accountable human.
units.responsibilityConflict: External write-through immediately changes AWSCURRENT for every external consumer without an approval/action digest in the provider contract. Rollback records two version ids but does not prove AWSCURRENT still equals the version Company OS wrote; a concurrent enterprise rotation could be overwritten. The error object retains raw provider text containing account/ARN metadata, and selected vault config permits no KMS key despite the default health path treating KMS as required.
